about: Recipes for the ship's observation table (backend/canary/data/observations.csv). One recipe per indicator, kept apart from the code. Anything that is not a published number is labelled 'prototype assumption' with verified=false and is listed in data/DATASET.md. Edit this file, run `python data/generate_dataset.py`, commit the result.

wearable.label: Wristband
wearable.how: A medical-grade wristband worn day and night. Photoplethysmography gives pulse, heart-rate variability, blood oxygen and sleep stages; skin temperature comes from a thermistor; an accelerometer and a proximity beacon give exercise minutes and time spent near crewmates. It syncs to the ship server over the cabin network every few minutes, with no action from the astronaut. Gaps appear when the band is charging or taken off.

manual.label: Cuff, scale and app questionnaires
manual.how: The astronaut does it and types or confirms the number in the app: blood pressure with an arm cuff, body mass on the ship's mass-measurement device (a scale does not work in 0 g), fasting glucose with a fingerstick meter, water from the dispenser log, mood, stress and sleepiness scales, workload questionnaire. Each takes under a minute. Missing days are normal and are never filled in silently.

test.label: Test in the app
test.how: A short task on the tablet: a one-minute reaction test, a digit-symbol and a digit-span task, a grip-strength reading from a Bluetooth dynamometer. The app times the answers itself, so nothing is typed. Bone density has no scanner on board: the bone row is a model estimate until an onboard measurement exists.

blood.label: Onboard blood analyser
blood.how: A fingerstick sample (about 100 µL) goes into a compact point-of-care analyser that returns a blood count and a chemistry panel in minutes. The crew medical officer runs it on a fixed calendar, about every 30 days, and the results go to the crew member's record. Hormones and vitamin D need a cartridge test or a sample returned to Earth.

urine.label: Urine analysis
urine.how: A 24-hour collection with a urine volume gauge and a dipstick or cartridge reader for calcium. Done about every 15 days. It is the early warning for kidney stones and for bone mineral leaving the body.

environment.label: Cabin sensors
environment.how: Fixed sensors in the habitat measure carbon dioxide continuously and report to the environment-control system. The numbers belong to the cabin, not to a person, so the rows use the crew id 'cabin'.

fatigue.label: Fatigue
fatigue.about: Tiredness that shows up in sleep, reaction time, mood, stress, time with the crew, cognition, sleepiness and workload at once.
fatigue.assumption: Slow personal wobble of 0.05 units with a 21-day period, so the state is never perfectly flat. The size is a prototype choice, small enough not to change any alert.

hydration.label: Hydration
hydration.about: How well watered the body is. Negative means dehydrated.
hydration.assumption: Same slow wobble as fatigue (0.05 units, 21 days).

energy.label: Energy balance
energy.about: Food intake against use. Moves body mass and fasting glucose together.
energy.assumption: Same slow wobble as fatigue. No dated event pushes this state yet.

bone_loss.label: Bone loss
bone_loss.about: Cumulative % of weight-bearing bone density lost since launch. It grows day by day with the gravity of the mission plan.
bone_loss.source: NASA: weight-bearing bones lose on average 1% to 1.5% of mineral density per month in spaceflight (nasa.gov, The Human Body in Space), https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/the-human-body-in-space/
bone_loss.assumption: 0.35% a month with full exercise (110 min a day) up to 1% a month without; full rate in 0 g, 40% in partial gravity, slow recovery (-25%) on Earth. Order of magnitude only, to verify before quoting.

events.label: Helena's slow slide on the way to Mars (days 132 to 153), then recovery
events.assumption: Written to drive the demo, not taken from data.

events.label: Tomás has space sickness on days 1 to 6: dehydrated, fast pulse, little exercise
events.assumption: Written to drive the demo, not taken from data.

sleep.assumption: Fictional personal baseline and day-to-day spread from catalog.py; fatigue effect (-1.5 h per unit) chosen for the demo story.

react.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; fatigue effect (+70 ms per unit) chosen for the demo story.

mood.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; fatigue (-1.2) and hydration (+0.6) effects chosen for the demo story.

stress.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; fatigue effect (+1.1 per unit) chosen for the demo story.

social.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; fatigue effect (-38 min per unit) chosen for the demo story.

hr.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; +12 bpm that fades over the 30 days after arriving in partial gravity, and a hydration effect (-12 bpm per unit) chosen for the demo story.

bp.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; -14 mmHg that fades over the 30 days after arriving in partial gravity. Daily, not every few days: the alert engine blends three days, and with a cuff reading every 3 days the demo's day-222 alerts changed.

spo2.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py.

temp.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py.

gluc.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; energy effect (+3 mg/dL per unit) is a prototype choice. Open real data exists (Inspiration4 metabolic panel) and can replace these rows through data/real/.

water.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; hydration effect (+1.1 L per unit) chosen for the demo story.

exer.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; hydration effect (+50 min per unit); during launch days exercise is capped at 25 to 35 min because there is little room to train.

grip.assumption: Fictional baseline and spread from catalog.py; -3 kg that fades over the 30 days after arriving in partial gravity. Daily, not weekly, for the same reason: a weekly reading changes the day-222 alerts.

vo2.assumption: Aerobic capacity (VO2max). Fictional baselines from catalog.py; a slow loss in 0 g of 0.015 mL/kg/min a day, a slower gain in partial gravity and a recovery on Earth, never more than 10 below the baseline. NASA-STD-3001 notes that aerobic capacity can be about 10% to 30% lower after flight (rationale of V1 4004); the daily rate here is a prototype choice.

bone.row_note: model estimate, no scanner on board
bone.source: NASA: weight-bearing bones lose on average 1% to 1.5% of mineral density per month in spaceflight (nasa.gov, The Human Body in Space), https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/the-human-body-in-space/
bone.assumption: Estimated % change of weight-bearing bone density since launch from the bone_loss state, plus 0.3 % of measurement noise (0.4 % before launch). The catalog's sd of 1.5 is the alert scale, not this noise. Daily because it is a model estimate, not a scan.

dsst.assumption: Digit-symbol substitution task, 60 s as in the app. Baselines, spread and fatigue effect (-12 per unit) are prototype choices; no real distribution was checked.

span.assumption: Digit span task. Baselines, spread and fatigue effect (-1 digit per unit) are prototype choices.

kss.assumption: Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (1 to 9). Baselines, spread and fatigue effect (+2 per unit) are prototype choices.

tlx.assumption: NASA-TLX workload questionnaire. Baselines, spread and fatigue effect (+14 per unit) are prototype choices.

hrv.assumption: Heart-rate variability (RMSSD). Baselines, spread and a slow drift down in space (up to -6 ms) are prototype choices.

weight.assumption: Body mass. Baselines, spread, energy effect and a slow loss in space (up to -4 kg) are prototype choices; the catalog only says weight loss is common.

creatinine.assumption: Real Inspiration4 values (OSD-575) on the 7 collections; between them, simulated rows around the person's real pre-flight mean and spread. The hydration effect (-0.12 mg/dL per unit) is a prototype choice.

potassium.assumption: Real Inspiration4 values (OSD-575) on the 7 collections; between them, simulated rows around the person's real pre-flight mean and spread.

crp.assumption: C-reactive protein, real Inspiration4 values (OSD-575 cardiovascular multiplex, pg/mL converted to mg/L); between collections, simulated rows around the person's real pre-flight mean and spread, never below 0.05 mg/L.

calcium.assumption: Real Inspiration4 values (OSD-575) on the 7 collections; between them, simulated rows around the person's real pre-flight mean and spread, flat on purpose because the body keeps serum calcium stable while bone and urine change.

cortisol.assumption: Baselines, spread and fatigue effect (+2 ug/dL per unit) are prototype choices.

vitamin_d.assumption: Baselines, spread and a slow fall without sunlight (up to -10 ng/mL) are prototype choices.

tsh.assumption: Baselines and spread are prototype choices; no effect of the mission.

urine_calcium.assumption: Baselines, spread and the link to bone loss (+40 mg/24h per % lost) are prototype choices.

urine_volume.assumption: Baselines, spread and hydration effect (+400 mL per unit) are prototype choices.

co2.subject: cabin
co2.assumption: Cabin carbon dioxide by place. Every level and the spread are prototype choices, not station or habitat specifications.
